text: "The Lord your God will set you high above all nations… and all these blessings shall come upon you." Position comes before blessing.
explanation:
Before Deuteronomy 28 lists a single blessing, it states a position: God sets His people high above. Only then do the blessings "come upon you and overtake you." That's a picture of where you are in Christ. "Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly places in Christ."

So don't live earthbound, as if you're limited to what's in your bank account or what your boss decides to pay you. You're seated with Christ, far above every name that is named. Take your place there, and let the blessings find you.

text: Peter put the mourners out, knelt down and prayed, and only then turned to the body and said, "Tabitha, arise."
explanation:
Tabitha, a woman full of good works, died in Joppa, whose name means beautiful: death had come into a place of beauty. The widows crowded around Peter, weeping and showing the garments she'd made, as if her good deeds might earn a miracle. But healing is a grace gift, never wages. Peter did what he'd seen Jesus do in Jairus' house: "Peter put them all out, and knelt down and prayed. And turning to the body he said, 'Tabitha, arise.'"

When death touches your situation, follow the same order. Put out the negative voices, the endless bad news and the doubting talk. Pray. Then turn to the situation and speak to it in Jesus' name. "It became known throughout all Joppa, and many believed on the Lord."

text: Both Tabitha and the Shunammite's son were laid in an upper room. When death strikes, bring it into the place of anointing.
explanation:
The Shunammite woman built a small room on her roof for Elisha. When her miracle son died, she didn't wail or make funeral plans. She carried him up, laid him on the man of God's bed, shut the door, and went to find Elisha. Asked, "Is it well with the child?" she answered, "It is well." Shalom. Not a lie, but faith that it shall be well.

When something precious seems to be dying, whether a child drifting, a marriage or your health, expose it to the anointing. Keep hearing the Word. Surround your children with it: play it in the car, and use your God-given authority in your home lovingly. The child was raised between the anointing above and the anointing beneath.

text: "He who would love life and see good days, let him refrain his tongue from evil."
explanation:
Is it biblical to want good days? Peter says so, and tells you where to start: your tongue. You can't author fear and doom in your speech and expect beautiful days to follow.

Interestingly, the Hebrew word for pestilence in Psalm 91, dever, shares its letters with davar, word. There's a link between what we say and what we experience. If you want to love life in the coming year, watch your words. Speak blessing over your body, your family and your future.

text: When his own brother mocked him, David "turned from him." Learn to turn away from the naysayers.
explanation:
As David asked about Goliath, his eldest brother Eliab burned with anger: "I know your pride and the insolence of your heart." David didn't stay to argue. "What have I done now? Is there not a cause?" Then "he turned from him toward another," and kept moving toward his giant.

You can't see good days while marinating in negativity. Turn away from critics who question your motives. Turn off the drama that's fearful from start to finish. Stop scrolling from one piece of bad news to the next. Turn your face toward what God has said.

text: Peter stayed "many days in Joppa with Simon, a tanner." Two Simons, "hearing," in the place called "beautiful."
explanation:
The chapter ends with this quiet detail: Peter stayed many days in Joppa, the beautiful place, at the house of Simon the tanner. Simon comes from shema, to hear, and here there are two of them: Simon Peter and Simon the tanner. Hearing and hearing. A tanner works with hides, turning raw flesh into leather.

It pictures the hearing that brings many beautiful days: not a hearing of the flesh, in one ear and out the other, but hearing mixed with faith. Israel heard God's word in the wilderness, "but the word which they heard did not profit them, not being mixed with faith." As you hear, say in your heart, "This is for me." Faith comes by hearing, and hearing.
